title: From Gene Copy to Protein Chain

scenes.tts: A plant or animal cell keeps its chromosomes inside the nucleus. How can their instructions reach a ribosome outside? Watch the blue D N A row remain behind while a green copy begins to grow.
scenes.caption: A plant or animal cell keeps its chromosomes inside the nucleus. How can their instructions reach a ribosome outside? Watch the blue DNA row remain behind while a green copy begins to grow.
scenes.visual: A single large cartoon cell fills the frame. A dark nucleus holds a wide row of blue letter blocks labelled DNA. Outside, an empty gold ribosome waits. A dotted path links them while the DNA blocks gently pulse. COLOR MAP: DNA blue; mRNA green; ribosome gold; tRNA purple; amino acids red.
scenes.narration: A plant or animal cell keeps its chromosomes inside the nucleus. How can their instructions reach a ribosome outside? Watch the blue DNA row remain behind while a green copy begins to grow.

scenes.visual: Keep the same cell faintly visible. Set the title 'From Gene Copy to Protein Chain' over it, then clear the title while the blue DNA remains in place.

scenes.tts: Making a protein from a gene is protein synthesis. The first stage is transcription. An enzyme opens a short stretch of D N A. It uses the template strand to build messenger R N A. Only the selected gene is copied.
scenes.caption: Making a protein from a gene is protein synthesis. The first stage is transcription. An enzyme opens a short stretch of DNA. It uses the template strand to build messenger RNA. Only the selected gene is copied.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the blue DNA row. A simple teal enzyme clamp opens only a highlighted gene segment. Green mRNA blocks appear beneath that segment from left to right. The rest of the DNA stays closed and dim, but never leaves the nucleus.
scenes.narration: Making a protein from a gene is protein synthesis. The first stage is transcription. An enzyme opens a short stretch of DNA. It uses the template strand to build messenger RNA. Only the selected gene is copied.

scenes.tts: Each green R N A block pairs with a blue D N A block. D N A letter A pairs with R N A letter U. T pairs with A. C pairs with G, and G pairs with C. R N A uses U instead of T.
scenes.caption: Each green RNA block pairs with a blue DNA block. DNA letter A pairs with RNA letter U. T pairs with A. C pairs with G, and G pairs with C. RNA uses U instead of T.
scenes.visual: Carry the open gene forward. Show large blue template blocks moving under the stationary enzyme clamp. Matching green blocks snap into a row beneath them. A compact pairing key appears only as each match happens, then shrinks beside the row.
scenes.narration: Each green RNA block pairs with a blue DNA block. DNA letter A pairs with RNA letter U. T pairs with A. C pairs with G, and G pairs with C. RNA uses U instead of T.

scenes.tts: Try the next template group. The blue D N A blocks read T A C. Which green messenger R N A blocks will pair with them? Keep the pairing key in view and choose the full group.
scenes.caption: Try the next template group. The blue DNA blocks read TAC. Which green messenger RNA blocks will pair with them? Keep the pairing key in view and choose the full group.
scenes.visual: Center three large blue template blocks labelled T, A and C. Beneath them place three empty green outlines. Keep the pairing key at the side. A question mark travels slowly across the empty positions.
scenes.narration: Try the next template group. The blue DNA blocks read TAC. Which green messenger RNA blocks will pair with them? Keep the pairing key in view and choose the full group.

scenes.visual: Hold the TAC blocks, empty green outlines and question. The question mark continues a slow loop so the deliberate thinking pause is not frozen.

scenes.tts: T pairs with A. A pairs with U. C pairs with G. The messenger group is A U G. The enzyme releases the finished message. The green strand peels away, while the blue D N A closes and stays inside.
scenes.caption: T pairs with A. A pairs with U. C pairs with G. The messenger group is AUG. The enzyme releases the finished message. The green strand peels away, while the blue DNA closes and stays inside.
scenes.visual: Fill the green outlines with A, U and G one at a time. Extend that group into the completed green strand. The strand peels upward from the template. The blue DNA closes behind the enzyme and settles in the nucleus.
scenes.narration: T pairs with A. A pairs with U. C pairs with G. The messenger group is AUG. The enzyme releases the finished message. The green strand peels away, while the blue DNA closes and stays inside.

scenes.tts: The messenger R N A passes through a pore into the cytoplasm. Translation begins when a gold ribosome grips the message. It reads each codon in order. A codon is a group of three letters that means an amino acid or stop.
scenes.caption: The messenger RNA passes through a pore into the cytoplasm. Translation begins when a gold ribosome grips the message. It reads each codon in order. A codon is a group of three letters that means an amino acid or stop.
scenes.visual: Zoom back to the whole cell. Pull the green strand through a bright pore into the cytoplasm. The gold ribosome closes around it. On screen, dividers group the message into sets of 3. The strip advances one codon at a time.
scenes.narration: The messenger RNA passes through a pore into the cytoplasm. Translation begins when a gold ribosome grips the message. It reads each codon in order. A codon is a group of three letters that means an amino acid or stop.

scenes.tts: Purple transfer R N A brings the amino acid matched to each codon. Its anticodon pairs with the codon inside the ribosome. The ribosome joins each red amino acid to the growing chain. At a stop codon, no amino acid is added and the chain is released.
scenes.caption: Purple transfer RNA brings the amino acid matched to each codon. Its anticodon pairs with the codon inside the ribosome. The ribosome joins each red amino acid to the growing chain. At a stop codon, no amino acid is added and the chain is released.
scenes.visual: Carry the ribosome and strip forward. Purple key-shaped tRNA cartoons arrive, pair briefly, and leave. Each delivers one labelled red amino-acid circle to a growing chain above. At a STOP block, no tRNA fits; the chain lifts free.
scenes.narration: Purple transfer RNA brings the amino acid matched to each codon. Its anticodon pairs with the codon inside the ribosome. The ribosome joins each red amino acid to the growing chain. At a stop codon, no amino acid is added and the chain is released.

scenes.tts: Reading usually begins at the start codon A U G. It adds methionine and fixes the grouping that follows. The ribosome then moves codon by codon. At U G A, the stop sign appears, the reading window opens, and the finished chain floats free.
scenes.caption: Reading usually begins at the start codon AUG. It adds methionine and fixes the grouping that follows. The ribosome then moves codon by codon. At UGA, the stop sign appears, the reading window opens, and the finished chain floats free.
scenes.visual: Mark AUG on the carried green strip with a START flag. Lock the codon dividers into place from that point. Move the gold ribosome across the strip. At UGA, transform that codon into a STOP sign and open the ribosome around the released chain.
scenes.narration: Reading usually begins at the start codon AUG. It adds methionine and fixes the grouping that follows. The ribosome then moves codon by codon. At UGA, the stop sign appears, the reading window opens, and the finished chain floats free.

scenes.tts: The released chain can fold into a working protein. The message changed form, but its order guided every handoff. In protein-coding genes, D N A order sets m R N A codons and amino acid order. That is how instructions inside the nucleus reach a protein outside.
scenes.caption: The released chain can fold into a working protein. The message changed form, but its order guided every handoff. In protein-coding genes, DNA order sets mRNA codons and amino acid order. That is how instructions inside the nucleus reach a protein outside.
scenes.visual: The red chain folds into a simple labelled protein blob, not a molecular structure. Draw a moving path from the blue DNA row to the green codon strip to the red chain. Each object stays large and in the same colour.
scenes.narration: The released chain can fold into a working protein. The message changed form, but its order guided every handoff. In protein-coding genes, DNA order sets mRNA codons and amino acid order. That is how instructions inside the nucleus reach a protein outside.

scenes.visual: Fade to one centered line only: 'In protein-coding genes, DNA order sets mRNA codons and amino acid order.' Keep the line large and still; show no subtitle, title or smaller line.
